cands.bio: Sean Kirrane is a Republican and entrepreneur who was the 2026 nominee for New Jersey's 5th Congressional District. He says he has worked as an executive in healthcare, finance and technology, starting at Hudson United Bank. He has not held public office.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Sean Kirrane grew up or when he began living in New Jersey; he calls himself a lifelong New Jerseyan, but no page gives details. His career history comes from his own survey answers and Ballotpedia, with no independent news coverage. We found no stated positions on data centers, development or land use, homestead property taxes, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties. The Ballotpedia survey text was cut off partway through, so any later answers were not read. He has held no office, so there are no official actions to report.

cands.bio: U.S. representative for New Jersey's 5th District since 2017. Born in Livingston, NJ. Harvard Law graduate. Former Clinton White House speechwriter, Ford and Microsoft executive, and senior adviser at the FCC. Ran for governor in 2025 and finished fourth in the Democratic primary.
cands.gaps: We found no documented position from him on data centers or on new development and land use. We found nothing on foreign-buyer limits for homes and land, school choice or teacher pay, or H-1B. The Wikipedia page we read was cut off partway through the immigration section, so anything after that was not read. We did not find a documented stance from him on state homeschool or voucher policy. Several of his positions come from the Wikipedia summary rather than a primary record.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

qual.background: Nine years in the U.S. House (since 2017), with a Harvard law degree. Earlier he was a Clinton White House speechwriter, a Ford Motor Company communications director, an executive at a PR firm, senior adviser to the FCC chairman, and a Microsoft strategist.
qual.why: Prior legislative office in the same body, plus a law degree and policy experience in federal agencies and in business.
qual.label: Prior legislative office in the same body, plus a law degree and policy experience in federal agencies and in business.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: In his 2025 run for governor he called for a 15% reduction in property taxes.

second-amendment.evidence: Voted for the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and against the Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act.

pro-life.evidence: Voted for the Women's Health Protection Act and the Ensuring Access to Abortion Act, and against the Supporting Pregnant and Parenting Women and Families Act. He introduced the Freedom to Decide Act and the SAFE Act on IVF access.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Nay on the Secure the Border Act of 2023, which would have limited asylum eligibility and required employers to use electronic work-eligibility verification.

back-police-order.evidence: Introduced the bipartisan Invest to Protect Act, which would create a grant program for police departments with fewer than 200 officers.

controversies.text: Federal records show $27,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $800,090 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate; 2 staff trips paid for by that foundation.
This Congress, Gottheimer missed 85 of 676 House votes (12.6%) through Sept. 16, 2026, including 16 in a row from June 4 to 11, 2025. He ran for governor in 2025.
